tasks.title: Refresh tokens
tasks.desc: Login returns a short-lived access token plus a refresh token, and a new endpoint swaps a valid refresh token for a new pair (rotating it). Done when an integration test shows an expired access token can be renewed and a used refresh token is rejected.

notes.text: Plan: read the current JWT login flow, then add rotating refresh tokens stored hashed in PostgreSQL, a refresh endpoint, and integration tests. Work on branch feat/refresh-tokens.

Login now returns a refresh token (valid 7 days) next to the access token, and the new POST /api/v1/auth/refresh swaps it for a fresh pair. Each refresh token works exactly once.

How it was verified: full `mvnw verify` passes (76 tests, PostgreSQL via Testcontainers). New integration tests show an expired access token being renewed, a used refresh token getting 401, and 10 simultaneous refreshes with one token where exactly one succeeds.

What to check:
- Try it in Swagger UI: log in, copy `refreshToken`, call /auth/refresh twice with it; the second call must answer 401.
- Response shape changed: login and refresh now also return `refreshToken` and `refreshExpiresIn` (seconds). Existing clients keep working, they just ignore the new fields.
- Lifetime is set by `wallet.security.refresh-token.ttl` (default 7d).

Decision for you: when a used token is presented again (a sign it was stolen), it is only rejected. Revoking every token of that user in that case fits better in SC-02 (revocation). Agree?

Branch feat/refresh-tokens, nothing committed yet. README (EN and ES) updated.

tasks.title: Token revocation and logout
tasks.desc: A user can log out, which invalidates their refresh token, and revoked tokens stop working before they expire. Done when an integration test shows a logged-out token is refused.

tasks.title: Currency conversion between wallets
tasks.desc: A user can move money between two of their own wallets in different currencies, at a rate from a rate service such as fx-rate-service behind an outbound port. The rate used is stored in the ledger. Done when a conversion keeps both ledgers balanced and is idempotent like any other movement.

notes.text: Plan: add a conversion movement (POST /api/v1/conversions) between two of the user's own wallets. Rate comes from fx-rate-service through a new outbound port; the rate and its date are stored on the transaction. Same idempotency and retry rules as transfers. Work on branch feat/currency-conversion (separate worktree, so SC-01's checkout is untouched).

tasks.title: Clean up old idempotency keys
tasks.desc: A scheduled job deletes idempotency keys older than 24 hours, so the table stops growing. Done when a test shows old keys are removed, recent ones are kept, and the job is safe to run on several instances.

tasks.title: Publish transaction events
tasks.desc: Every completed deposit, withdrawal or transfer writes an event to an outbox table in the same database transaction, and a relay publishes it afterwards. Done when no event is lost or duplicated if the app crashes between the commit and the publish.

tasks.title: Metrics and tracing
tasks.desc: Micrometer metrics (movements, failures, retries) and OpenTelemetry traces for each request. Done when the metrics endpoint shows them and a trace follows a transfer through the database call.
